slides.title: 5 myths about the little details on your stuff

slides.myth: The color square on a toothpaste tube tells you what's in it.
slides.fact: It's an eye mark. A light sensor on the packaging line reads it to find where to cut and seal the tube. The color only has to stand out.

slides.myth: The hole in a pot lid is for a meat thermometer.
slides.fact: Usually it lets a little steam out and keeps the lid from rattling. Some slow cooker models do have a probe hole, so check your manual.

slides.myth: It's illegal to cut the tag off your pillow.
slides.fact: The "do not remove" warning is aimed at sellers, not you. Once it's yours, you can remove it.

slides.myth: Mattress handles are for carrying it.
slides.fact: Serta says handles are designed to position the mattress only. Simmons says carrying by the handles can tear the fabric.

slides.myth: The cup that comes with a rice cooker is a US cup.
slides.fact: It holds about 180 milliliters, roughly three quarters of a US cup. The water lines in the pot are marked for it.
